records.title: Domestic holy-water font / bénitier de chevet
records.claim_boundary: Material culture directly establishes the bedside holy-water vessel; document what the museum object shows, not the prevalence of domestic prayer.

p2_source_text_review.claim_supported: Six Mucem catalog results include French bedside holy-water fonts from 1900–1925 and 1950.
p2_source_text_review.remaining_hold: Objects prove historical household vessels, not rates of use or a universal prayer routine.

records.title: Family consecration to the Sacred Heart
records.claim_boundary: Paray sanctuary supports voluntary family consecration; priestly or parish ceremonies must remain separate from household prayer.

p2_source_text_review.claim_supported: Paray sanctuary describes voluntary family consecration, daily renewal and Jesuit promotion since 1870.
p2_source_text_review.remaining_hold: Some consecrations take place during Mass; this does not create a universal 1962 Mass ceremony.

records.title: Intronement of a Sacred Heart image in the home
records.claim_boundary: Paray sanctuary supports enthroning a Sacred Heart image; do not imply mandatory blessing or universal ritual.

p2_source_text_review.claim_supported: Paray describes family enthronement of an image and its relation to consecration.
p2_source_text_review.remaining_hold: Attributed devotional promises are not verified outcomes or compulsory ministerial blessings.

records.title: Relevailles / blessing after childbirth
records.claim_boundary: Historical post-childbirth blessing must not be described as purifying impurity, imposing forty days or excluding the mother from worship.

p1_source_text_review.finding: Traditional 40-day timing is attested as imitation of the Presentation; not evidence for an obligatory waiting period, maternal impurity or a bar to entering church.

records.title: May as the month of Mary
records.claim_boundary: French bishops directly describe May devotion as popular piety, not a new Roman liturgical season.

records.title: Pilgrimage to a shrine or holy place
records.claim_boundary: The Directory establishes pilgrimage in general; the numerous locally dated shrine witnesses vary in accessibility and may not establish today's schedule.

p1_source_text_review.finding: 2001 Vatican Directory treats pilgrimage as popular piety. Does not verify each 2025/2026 shrine event or universal 1962 pilgrimage schedule.

records.title: Ex-votos
records.claim_boundary: Laghet demonstrates shrine ex-votos; Altötting page was access-inconclusive and requires later browser validation.

p2_source_text_review.claim_supported: Laghet sanctuary indexed page reports over 4,000 ex-votos and historical thanksgiving objects.
p2_source_text_review.remaining_hold: Direct live page timed out; no verification of every alleged miracle or artwork reuse rights.

followup_primary_source_verification.finding: The sanctuary's own readable text reports more than 4,000 ex-votos; the collection is thanksgiving evidence, not automatic adjudication of all miracle claims.
followup_primary_source_verification.remaining_hold: Art reuse, material-object rights, and reports of individual cures remain unverified.

records.title: Votive candle at a shrine
records.claim_boundary: Shrine candles are devotional offerings, never payments for spiritual effects; some cited local offers are dated or not always accessible.

p1_source_text_review.finding: Lourdes shrine explicitly presents lighting a candle as extending a pilgrim's prayer. No universal prices or spiritual effects can be inferred.

records.title: Prayerful cemetery visit
records.claim_boundary: Distinguish prayer at cemeteries from an assumed local indulgence or universally required November visit.

p2_source_text_review.claim_supported: Directory §260 describes public and private cemetery visits; French bishops note many Catholics tending graves on 2 November.
p2_source_text_review.remaining_hold: No duty arising from superstition, guaranteed indulgence or compulsory local date.

records.title: Prayer for the dead on 2 November
records.claim_boundary: 2 November liturgical commemoration is separate from Polish wypominki parish custom and local prayer schedules.

p2_source_text_review.claim_supported: French bishops identify 2 November intercession for the dead; Directory §255–260 discusses Mass and prayer.
p2_source_text_review.remaining_hold: Polish wypominki and local memorial services require distinct regional attestation.

records.title: Using holy water at home
records.claim_boundary: Blessing holy water is a reserved rite; use of already blessed water in the home is lay devotion distinct from the DOM-002 vessel.

p2_source_text_review.claim_supported: Weller Roman Ritual index establishes historical blessings; Mucem artifacts establish domestic holy-water vessels.
p2_source_text_review.remaining_hold: Ritual index alone does not prove frequency of personal routines; lay users do not confer reserved blessings.

followup_primary_source_verification.finding: Rev. David O'Connor explicitly documents holy water taken from church, home door/bedroom fonts and personal Sign of Cross, separately from priestly water blessing.
followup_primary_source_verification.remaining_hold: This is a priestly pastoral attestation, not a census of historical frequency or authorization to enact the reserved blessing.

records.title: Keeping blessed Candlemas candles at home
records.claim_boundary: Original French liturgical lexicon explicitly says blessed Candlemas candles are taken home and traditionally burned 'auprès des morts' (beside the deceased), NOT 'auprès des mourants' (beside the dying); corresponding EN/FR article, folio and source-registry text corrected.

p1_source_text_review.finding: The French liturgical lexicon says candles were traditionally burned auprès des morts, beside the deceased, not mourants (dying); article, folio and registry corrected.

records.title: Keeping blessed Palm Sunday branches at home
records.claim_boundary: Keep blessed Palm branches and home crucifix custom distinct from 1962 liturgical blessing/procession; exclude magical claims.

p2_source_text_review.claim_supported: Directory §139 explicitly documents keeping blessed greenery at home and warns against amuletic use.
p2_source_text_review.remaining_hold: No mandated plant, placement, talisman effect or 1962 rubric change.

records.title: St Blaise — blessing of throats
records.claim_boundary: Traditional Roman Ritual and modern Book of Blessings use different formulas and ministerial permissions; do not conflate them or infer treatment of illness.

p1_source_text_review.finding: Philip T Weller's Roman Ritual transcription has a blessing of candles specifically for St Blaise, followed by the blessing with crossed candles; distinguish from the modern Book of Blessings.

records.title: Baptismal patron's name day
records.claim_boundary: Personal baptismal patron must be chosen or known; source attests family name-day celebrations but not automatic feast lookup from a first name.

p2_source_text_review.claim_supported: Helen McLoughlin's 1962 approved handbook details nameday family celebration, dessert, prayer and optional Mass.
p2_source_text_review.remaining_hold: A first name does not identify a patron automatically; copyrighted 1962 book is not for wholesale republication.

records.title: French fête patronale / village patronal celebration
records.claim_boundary: French bishops explicitly attest Chantelle patronal feast after Ascension and relic procession; locality cannot set national feast date.

records.title: French Assumption Marian processions
records.claim_boundary: Paris 2026 Assumption announcement attests a named procession; no countrywide or annual event availability inferred.

p2_source_text_review.claim_supported: Paris diocese specifies Notre-Dame processions on 14 and 15 August 2026.
p2_source_text_review.remaining_hold: Dated Paris event is not a default procession elsewhere or a future-year schedule.

records.title: St Joseph's table and gifts to the poor
records.claim_boundary: 2026 diocesan St Joseph altar witnesses charitable sharing; a single US celebration is not definitive documentation of Sicilian historical origin.

p1_source_text_review.finding: 19 March 2026 Baton Rouge diocesan account explicitly identifies Sicilian Catholic roots, St Joseph food altar, charitable purpose and local parish blessing; it does not establish an exact medieval foundation.

records.title: St Anthony's Bread / Pain des pauvres
records.claim_boundary: Sanctuary documents Louise Bouffier and 1890 Toulon revival; associated miracle tradition is not independently certified.

records.title: St Christopher — vehicles and travellers' blessing
records.claim_boundary: Laval vehicle blessing is a local 2026 event and no assurance of future availability or safety.

p2_source_text_review.claim_supported: Laval parish scheduled 11 AM Mass and noon vehicle blessing at Saint-Christophe-du-Luat on 19 July 2026.
p2_source_text_review.remaining_hold: The attested celebration was 19 July, not 25 July; no annually repeated service or physical safety guarantee.

records.title: St Nicholas's visit and small gifts to children
records.claim_boundary: Strasbourg source attests regional St Nicholas visits and gifts; distinguish regional folklore from the historical bishop.

p2_source_text_review.claim_supported: Strasbourg diocesan 2022 text describes sweets, gifts and visits in Alsace and Lorraine.
p2_source_text_review.remaining_hold: Live fetch 502; later folklore and threatening companions are not saint biography or prescribed liturgy.

followup_primary_source_verification.finding: Full diocesan indexed article dated 6 Dec 2022 describes regional children's gifts and saints-day traditions, distinguishing the historic bishop from folklore; a diocesan parish report separately attests a 2016 local St Nicholas gift visit.
followup_primary_source_verification.remaining_hold: The 2022 original and the alternative parish page both returned HTTP 502 when opened directly; exact indexed content is available, but direct-origin access has not recovered.

records.title: Assumption — blessing of herbs, flowers and fruits
records.claim_boundary: Directory 181 locates Assumption herb blessing in Germanic regions; traditional ritual witness and current parish example are distinct.

p2_source_text_review.claim_supported: Directory §181 locates Assumption herb blessing especially in Germanic countries and refers to ritual incorporation.
p2_source_text_review.remaining_hold: Ministerial blessing remains optional and is not a universal rule.

records.title: St John the Evangelist — blessing of wine
records.claim_boundary: Separate traditional wine blessing, contemporary parish witness, non-Eucharistic nature, and the legendary poisoned-wine narrative.

p1_source_text_review.finding: Philip T Weller 1964 Roman Ritual transcription describes priest blessing wine on St John feast, after last Gospel. Legendary poison story belongs to ritual's explanatory account; not an established historical event or automatic local offering.

records.title: Holy Saturday — blessing of Easter foods
records.claim_boundary: Roman Ritual food blessings and Slavic-rooted Holy Saturday baskets must not be assumed identical or universally available.

p2_source_text_review.claim_supported: Catholic Culture supplies Weller Roman Ritual blessings for lamb, eggs and bread, distinct from Polish/Slovak basket witnesses.
p2_source_text_review.remaining_hold: 1952/1964 edition references do not by themselves certify the exact 1962 ritual text.

records.title: Family Advent wreath and Sunday candle prayer
records.claim_boundary: Published history was a duplicate; revised to documented Catholic home use. Köln 1839 Wichern and Catholic uptake sources remain proposed historical references, not yet registered.

p1_source_text_review.finding: Cologne archdiocese describes Wichern 1839 multi-candle model and later Catholic four-candle adoption; official historic source separately linked in published article.

records.title: Advent manger straw after acts of charity
records.claim_boundary: Single contemporary family description attributes manger straw to France; does not prove national or ancient French customary origin.

p1_source_text_review.finding: Cologne archdiocese also describes manger straw after good deeds in German Catholic regions; 2014 Catholic Culture French attribution is not proof of French-only origin.

records.title: Las Posadas — Holy Family lodging procession
records.claim_boundary: USCCB establishes living Las Posadas, not sole historical origin. Mexican Culture Ministry presents Acolman 1587 and Andalusian transmission as competing accounts.

p1_source_text_review.finding: Mexican Ministry of Culture explicitly gives Acolman 1587 and Andalusian transmission as rival origin accounts; do not choose an exclusive origin.

records.title: Sharing opłatek on Polish Christmas Eve
records.claim_boundary: Polish opłatek sharing is family bread, never Holy Communion; one diaspora parish cannot establish precise original date.

p2_source_text_review.claim_supported: Vermont Catholic parish describes Polish Christmas Eve opłatek as unconsecrated thin bread, distinct from the Eucharist.
p2_source_text_review.remaining_hold: Dated local blessing announcement does not establish future schedules.

records.title: Holy Thursday visits to altars of repose
records.claim_boundary: 2026 Catholic press supports voluntary Holy Thursday repose visits; St Philip Neri Roman seven-basilica pilgrimage is not established as identical origin.

p1_source_text_review.finding: Chicago Catholic March 2026 documents visits after Mass; St Philip Neri ancestry is attributed to what many say, not independent origin proof; no fixed seven-stop requirement.

records.title: Family Rogation walk and prayer for the harvest
records.claim_boundary: Mid-twentieth-century family prayer walk is an optional adaptation, not the Roman Church's formal Rogation procession or a lay blessing rite.

p1_source_text_review.finding: Family guide proposes household processional prayer for crops, distinct from formal Church Rogations; does not authorize faithful to simulate prescribed blessings reserved to clergy.

records.title: German Epiphany star singers / Sternsinger
records.claim_boundary: Kindermissionswerk supports modern German charity singers, not the full medieval practice or guaranteed local house blessing.

records.title: French Galette des Rois and the poor person's portion
records.claim_boundary: French bishops directly describe galette, fève, paper crown and optional poor person's share; Roman antiquity and separate school-fees story not established.

records.title: Corpus Christi flower carpets and window decorations
records.claim_boundary: UNESCO supports Polish family flower carpets (inscribed 2021); other regional flower customs need distinct citations, no universal procession event.

records.title: Easter Monday Emmaus walk
records.claim_boundary: Archdiocesan account documents Bavarian Easter Monday Emmaus walks; neither historical start date nor 2026 parish itinerary generalizes.

p2_source_text_review.claim_supported: Munich–Freising indexed text describes southern German/Austrian Easter Monday Emmaus walks associated with Luke 24.
p2_source_text_review.remaining_hold: Direct article fetch timed out; no universal origin, precise inception or current parish itinerary.

followup_primary_source_verification.finding: Munich–Freising's current official 2026 press article directly documents an Easter Monday Emmaus walk in Ruhpolding on 6 April. It independently corroborates practice even though the original archived Emmausgang article timed out.
followup_primary_source_verification.remaining_hold: The original legacy URL remains intermittently inaccessible and the 2026 event cannot create perpetual or universal schedule.

records.title: Mary garden — flowers and herbs dedicated to Our Lady
records.claim_boundary: Catholic Culture documents contemporary Marian gardening; 1932 Woods Hole/1951 Philadelphia history is documented separately at Dayton, not yet registered.

p1_source_text_review.finding: Dayton Marian Library documents 1932 Woods Hole public garden and 1951 Philadelphia initiative; medieval Marian plant-name symbolism does not establish a medieval origin for modern formal garden layouts.
